# TypeScript strict patterns and best practices

Curated by Skill Harbor — @gentleman-programming's strict TypeScript patterns skill: opinionated discipline for the agent writing TypeScript. Const object created first with `as const`, type extracted via `(typeof X)[keyof typeof X]` — direct union types forbidden; interfaces kept one level deep with nested objects promoted to dedicated interfaces; `any` never used (use `unknown` for truly unknown data, generics for flexible functions); the full utility-type kit (`Pick`, `Omit`, `Partial`, `Required`, `Readonly`, `Record`, `Extract`, `Exclude`, `NonNullable`, `ReturnType`, `Parameters`); type guards with `value is User` narrowing; and `import type` conventions. Every rule is shown as ✅ always / ❌ never with code. Honest caveats: methodology only — the agent needs a TypeScript project (ideally strict mode) to apply it to; license is MIT per the catalog (the file's frontmatter also mentions Apache-2.0). Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
